study.question: Does content-aligned task-mask membership outperform count-preserving valid-history reassignment separately through native shared scorer normalization and through the auxiliary feedback readout, beyond aligned historical item fields/actions?
study.hypothesis: The observed full/counts gap can arise from normalization populations, auxiliary grouped readout, or their interaction. The g1-r0083 joint closure yields identical reported full/counts results, but this does not establish semantic utility in either path. If useful event assignment rather than frequency or generic grouped-value dispersion drives a path, full membership should exceed both counts-only and joint-pattern-preserving permutation in that matched path setting. The original action codes already determine task masks in the inspected loader, so this concerns representation and optimization utility, not new information.

study.proposed_difference: Use membership_use=permuted in a 2x2 normalization (native,row_local) by auxiliary readout (feedback,uniform) diagnostic suite. The common source permits inherited permutation and selects the two existing normalization implementations. Reuse the existing matched full/counts cells; the native permutation cell is a source bridge and the closed-path cell is an integrity null. No new parameter, running buffer, random stream, loss term, action policy, capacity or task label is added. This is continuation of an attribution trajectory, not a new architecture, novelty claim, accuracy improvement or a new seed replication.
predictions: Native permutation bridge should reproduce g1-r0078-membership_permuted at click AUC 0.6688852920320618 within host numerical repeatability, with identical parameter counts; exact tensor-level reproduction remains untested in this jail.

Both-paths-closed permutation should match the g1-r0083 full/counts click AUC 0.6677354125015613 and all four reported task metrics within numerical repeatability. At a common parameter state consumed forward/gradient paths should be identical; unused private auxiliary running buffers need not agree.

If alignment is useful on the normalization-only route, full g1-r0081 uniform_aux should exceed new native_uniform permutation and counts-only 0.6688764855097781. Its measured full/counts margin is only 0.0000134479024380, so any result remains preliminary.

If alignment is useful on the readout-only route, full g1-r0082 row_local should exceed new row_local_feedback permutation and counts-only 0.6676954846785449. Its measured full/counts margin is 0.0000582135067290.

Report the membership-effect interaction across normalization/readout cells using full minus permutation and full minus counts, rather than treating route contributions as additive. A permutation near full with both beating counts would implicate grouped-value variation rather than demonstrated semantic assignment.
falsifiers: Any introduced visibility of padded events, altered labels/actions/target, changed host recipe, capacity mismatch or broken per-block counts/joint-pattern preservation invalidates the contrast.
Failure of the native source bridge or a consumed-output discrepancy in the both-closed null prevents route attribution; do not label execution failure as scientific counterevidence.
Full membership failing to beat the permuted and counts-only representations undermines alignment-specific conditional utility for that matched path. No positive effect is assumed in advance.
A gain explained by extra parameters, training passes, memory or runtime does not establish a justified quality/cost improvement. Added permutation work must be measured.
A single frozen-seed difference, including one exceeding both controls, cannot establish repeated support or statistical significance.
